title: Tata Tiscon rebar range: 550, SD, Footing, Superlinks and CRS
body:
Tata Tiscon is Tata Steel's brand of TMT reinforcement bars (rebars) for houses, buildings and infrastructure. As of October 2026 the official product pages describe these products:

- Tata Tiscon 550: a high-strength ribbed TMT bar that gives consistent strength. It is meant for heavy-duty construction and can reduce the amount of steel needed.
- Tata Tiscon SD (Super Ductile), sold as SD 550D: combines high tensile strength with extra ductility, made for seismic-prone zones. Tata Steel calls it India's first GreenPro-certified rebar brand.
- Tata Tiscon SD 550D CRS: a corrosion-resistant version for coastal areas, brackish groundwater, moisture and polluted air.
- Tata Tiscon Footing: a ready-made rebar kit for footings that reduces site mistakes and speeds up work.
- Tata Tiscon Superlinks: ready-made stirrups made from ribbed TMT bars. They hold the main bars in place and stop them buckling.

Tata Steel makes Tiscon by the primary route (from iron ore and hot metal), in batches of 130 to 150 tonnes. Secondary-route mills usually work in batches of 3 to 10 tonnes. For heavy projects such as metro rail, tunnels and bridges, 36 mm and 40 mm bars are offered. Custom lengths of 7.5 m to 11.5 m, in 0.5 m steps, are also available.

The products are sold through Tata Tiscon dealers, the Tata Steel Aashiyana online store and shop.tatatiscon.co.in. Ask your dealer which diameters are in stock, because stock differs by state.

title: IS 1786 grades explained: Fe500, Fe500D and Fe550D
body:
All TMT bars sold in India are covered by the BIS standard IS 1786:2008, which sets the minimum strength and ductility for each grade. The number in the grade name is the minimum 0.2% proof (yield) stress in MPa. The letter D means the grade has higher ductility and tighter chemistry limits.

Minimum mechanical values in the standard:
- Fe500: yield 500 MPa, tensile strength at least 545 MPa, tensile/yield ratio at least 1.08, elongation at least 12%.
- Fe500D: yield 500 MPa, tensile strength at least 565 MPa, elongation at least 16%.
- Fe550D: yield 550 MPa, tensile strength at least 8% above the actual yield and never below 600 MPa (ratio 1.08), elongation at least 14.5%, and total elongation at maximum force (Agt) at least 5%.

Chemistry limits for the D grades (Fe500D and Fe550D): carbon up to 0.25%, sulphur up to 0.040%, phosphorus up to 0.040%, and sulphur plus phosphorus together up to 0.075%.

Which grade to choose: D grades bend more before they break, which helps in earthquake zones, where IS 13920 also applies. The structural engineer's drawing names the grade. Always buy the grade written on the drawing, and check that the grade on the bar and on the mill test certificate is the same.

These figures are a summary. For contract acceptance, refer to the current BIS text of IS 1786 and its amendments.

title: Tata Tiscon SD 550D: how it compares with IS 1786
body:
Tata Steel publishes its own specification for Tata Tiscon SD 550D, and it is tighter than the IS 1786 Fe550D minimums. As of October 2026 the published values are:

Mechanical
- Yield strength: at least 570 MPa and at most 660 MPa. IS 1786 Fe550D requires at least 550 MPa.
- Tensile/yield ratio: 1.15 to 1.25, with tensile strength at least 15% above yield and never below 655 MPa. IS 1786 requires a ratio of at least 1.08.
- Total elongation: at least 16%. IS 1786 requires 14.5%.
- Total elongation at maximum force (Agt): at least 5%, the same as IS 1786.

Chemical (maximum)
- Carbon: 0.25%
- Sulphur: 0.035%. IS 1786 allows 0.04%.
- Phosphorus: 0.035%. IS 1786 allows 0.04%.
- Sulphur plus phosphorus: 0.070%. IS 1786 allows 0.075%.

The ratio range of 1.15 to 1.25 and the cap on yield strength match IS 13920:2016, the Indian code for ductile detailing in earthquake zones. Tata Steel notes that about 55% of India's land area is vulnerable to earthquakes.

The CRS (corrosion-resistant) version has the same mechanical properties. It has lower carbon (0.20% max), carbon equivalent up to 0.45%, nitrogen up to 80 ppm, and at least 0.40% of copper, chromium, molybdenum, phosphorus and nickel combined.

To see the actual values for your material, ask for the mill test certificate by heat number.

title: When to use corrosion-resistant (CRS) rebars
body:
Tata Tiscon SD 550D CRS is a corrosion-resistant version of the SD 550D rebar. Small amounts of elements such as copper, chromium and nickel are added, at least 0.40% combined, and carbon is kept at or below 0.20%. This slows rusting in harsh conditions.

Tata Steel recommends CRS bars where concrete is exposed to:
- salty air near the sea, or sea water
- brackish or saline groundwater
- constant moisture, as in basements, water tanks and sewage plants
- acid particles from industrial emissions

As of October 2026, Tata Steel lists projects that used CRS rebars, including the Dholera semiconductor project and the Bandra sewage treatment plant.

The strength and ductility are the same as SD 550D: at least 570 MPa yield, tensile/yield ratio of 1.15 or more, and at least 16% elongation. You do not need to change the structural design for strength reasons. Your engineer should still specify CRS on the drawing and bill of quantities.

CRS bars do not replace good practice. You still need the correct concrete cover, good concrete quality and proper curing. Store bars off the ground and under cover until use.

To order, ask an authorised Tata Tiscon dealer, or write to the regional email for your zone listed in the contact article.

title: How to make sure you are buying genuine Tata Tiscon
body:
Fake and stolen material does turn up in the market. In September 2019, police in Jamshedpur raided a stockyard on a tip-off from Tata Steel Security and seized 1.5 tonnes of Tata Tiscon rebars that had been stolen in transit and sold through local traders. Tata Steel says it acts against anyone selling stolen or counterfeit Tata-branded steel.

Checks before you pay:
1. Buy from an authorised dealer. Use the Dealer Locator on tatatiscon.co.in to find verified dealers in your state and district, or buy on the Tata Steel Aashiyana store.
2. Look at the bar. Brand, grade and BIS marking should be rolled onto the bar. Check that the grade on the bar matches the grade you ordered.
3. Ask for a proper GST tax invoice from the dealer that shows the grade, the diameter and the weight.
4. Ask for the mill test certificate (MTC) for the heat numbers you receive. It shows the chemical and mechanical test results for that heat.
5. Be careful of prices well below the market rate, and of anyone who offers a 'dealership approval' for a fee.

If you doubt a dealer or a delivery, call the Tata Steel helpline 1800 108 8282 or raise a request through the Customer Service Request System on tatasteel.com before you use the material.

title: Mill test certificates (MTC): what they show and how to get one
body:
A mill test certificate, also called an MTC or test certificate, is the quality document for one heat (cast) of steel. Every bundle carries a heat number, and the MTC for that heat number gives the test results for that batch. Tata nexarc advises buyers to ask the supplier for the MTC to check the quality of TMT bars.

A rebar MTC normally shows:
- heat number, grade (for example Fe500D or Fe550D), diameter and the standard (IS 1786)
- chemical analysis: carbon, sulphur, phosphorus, sulphur plus phosphorus, and carbon equivalent
- mechanical tests: yield (0.2% proof) stress, tensile strength, tensile/yield ratio and elongation; for D grades, also total elongation at maximum force
- bend and rebend test result, and the test date

How to check it: compare each value with the minimums for your grade in the IS 1786 article. For Fe500D, for example, check that yield is at least 500 MPa, tensile strength at least 565 MPa, elongation at least 16%, carbon at most 0.25%, and sulphur plus phosphorus at most 0.075%.

How to get one: ask the dealer when you take delivery. In this portal, signed-in dealers and builders can look up the certificate for their own orders by heat number. Keep the MTC with the site quality records, because consultants and auditors often ask for it.

title: Buying Tata Steel products online on Aashiyana
body:
Tata Steel Aashiyana (aashiyana.tatasteel.com) is Tata Steel's online store for home builders. It sells Tata Tiscon rebars and Superlinks, Tata Wiron binding and fencing wire, Tata Structura hollow sections, Tata Durashine roofing sheets, Tata Pravesh doors and windows, Tiscobuild blocks and Agrico tools. It also has house plans, a rebar estimator and budget calculators.

How to order:
1. Log in or create an account.
2. Choose your state and district. Prices and stock depend on the location. If you change the location, the items in your cart are removed.
3. Pick the product and quantity, then check out.
4. At checkout, choose a delivery slot and a dealer near you, then choose how to pay.
5. Track the order under My Orders in your profile ('Track my order').

The delivery pincode must match the location you selected, or the site shows a 'Pincode Mismatch' message.

As of October 2026 you can also order on call at 0124-6934550, or email aashiyana.support@tatasteel.com. The Help & Support page has a chat assistant called Aashi and a call-back option.

Bulk project orders for builders and contractors usually go through an authorised dealer or distributor rather than the online store.

title: Aashiyana delivery times and shipping charges
body:
As of October 2026 the Aashiyana FAQ says:

- Tata Tiscon rebars are delivered free within 24 to 72 hours if the site is within 5 km of municipal limits.
- Tata Wiron orders below Rs 15,000 have to be collected from the dealer's counter.
- Shipping charges apply to Tata Structura, Tata Wiron and Tata Durashine. Shipping charges can also apply to Tata Tiscon in some states: the FAQ lists exceptions for West Bengal, Bihar, Jharkhand, Meghalaya, Assam, Mizoram, Tripura and Arunachal Pradesh. The FAQ is not fully consistent on this point, so check the charge shown at checkout or call support.

The dealer you pick at checkout delivers the material from their outlet. For a smooth delivery:
- give a site address the truck can reach, with a contact person on site
- arrange labour to unload, and a dry place to stack the bars off the ground
- count the bundles and check sizes against the invoice before signing

If the quantity or size is wrong, do not use the material. Report it through the helpline (see the returns article).

For orders placed through a dealer, check the expected dispatch date with the dealer. Signed-in dealers can see order and lorry receipt (LR) status in this portal.

title: Payment options on Aashiyana (no cash on delivery)
body:
As of October 2026, Tata Steel Aashiyana accepts:
- credit and debit cards (Visa, Mastercard, AMEX)
- net banking
- wallets and UPI apps, such as PayUMoney and Google Pay
- EMI on selected credit cards, including those of HDFC, ICICI, SBI, Axis and Kotak Mahindra Bank

Payment must be made before delivery. Cash on delivery is not available, and material is dispatched only after the payment is complete.

There are two order types, and they have different cancellation rules:
- Pay Now: you pay at checkout.
- Pay Before Dispatch: you pay before the dealer dispatches the material.

If money was deducted but the order does not show as placed, do not pay again straight away. Wait a short while and check My Orders. If it still does not appear, contact Aashiyana support at 0124-6934550 or aashiyana.support@tatasteel.com with the transaction reference.

Dealers and project buyers who buy on credit through an authorised distributor follow the payment terms agreed with that distributor. The portal cannot change those terms.

title: Cancelling an Aashiyana order and getting a refund
body:
As of October 2026, the Aashiyana FAQ sets these cancellation rules:

Pay Now orders
- You can cancel within 24 hours of placing the order, or before dispatch, whichever comes first.
- The refund goes to the original bank account or card after the standard payment gateway charge is deducted.
- An accepted refund can take up to 10 working days.
- Requests made after 24 hours, or after the material has been dispatched, are rejected.

Pay Before Dispatch orders
- You can cancel through the portal or the toll-free number before the dealer dispatches the material, or before you pay.
- Requests after that are rejected.

How to cancel: use My Orders on the Aashiyana site, or call 1800 108 8282 or 0124-6934550. Keep the order number ready.

If 10 working days have passed after an accepted cancellation and you have not received the refund, write to aashiyana.support@tatasteel.com with the order number and the date of cancellation.

title: Returns and replacements for delivered material
body:
As of October 2026, Aashiyana orders cannot be returned once delivered. This applies to both Pay Now and Pay Before Dispatch orders.

A replacement is possible only when:
- the delivered quantity differs from the order, or
- the delivered size or diameter differs from the order.

The material must be in the same form in which it was delivered. Bars that have been cut, bent, or tied into the structure cannot be replaced.

What to do:
1. Check the material at unloading, before you sign the delivery receipt. Count the bundles and check the diameter and grade marked on the bars.
2. Take photos of the bundle tags and of the bars.
3. Call 1800 108 8282 or 0124-6934550 with the order number and the photos.

For quality concerns, such as a bar that cracks in the bend test, do not use the affected heat. Note the heat number from the bundle tag, ask for the mill test certificate, and raise a complaint through the Customer Service Request System on tatasteel.com. Have the invoice ready, and note where you bought the material.

title: E-way bill for steel dispatches: what dealers and transporters need
body:
Under GST, goods worth more than Rs 50,000 in one consignment need an e-way bill to move. A truckload of steel almost always crosses this limit. The limit is the same for all interstate movement. For movement within a state, each state sets its own limit, between Rs 50,000 and Rs 2,00,000. These figures are as of October 2026.

The e-way bill has two parts:
- Part A: GSTIN of the recipient, delivery PIN code, invoice number and date, value, HSN code, and the reason for transport.
- Part B: vehicle (truck) number for road transport.
Part B can be skipped only when the goods move less than 50 km within the same state, between the supplier or buyer and the transporter.

How long it is valid (normal cargo): 1 day for up to 200 km, plus 1 day for each additional 200 km or part of it. Validity starts when Part B is first entered and ends at midnight on the last day. Over-dimensional cargo, such as very long structural sections, gets 1 day per 20 km.

Other points:
- The driver must carry the e-way bill number, on paper or on a phone, and the invoice.
- If the truck changes on the way, update Part B with the new vehicle number.
- A transporter can extend the validity within 8 hours before or after expiry, with a reason such as a breakdown.
- An e-way bill can be cancelled within 24 hours if it has not been verified by an officer.

The e-way bill number for each dispatch appears on the dispatch record in this portal.

title: GST e-invoice, IRN and QR code on steel invoices
body:
Since 1 August 2023, businesses with annual aggregate turnover above Rs 5 crore must issue e-invoices for B2B (business) and B2G (government) sales. This was notified in Notification 10/2023 – Central Tax, and still applies as of October 2026. Tata Steel and most distributors are well above this limit, so business buyers receive e-invoices.

How it works: the seller uploads the invoice details to the Invoice Registration Portal (IRP). The IRP checks the details and returns an Invoice Reference Number (IRN) and a signed QR code. The seller must print the IRN and the QR code on the invoice before giving it to the buyer.

Why it matters to you as a buyer:
- A B2B invoice from a business covered by e-invoicing is valid only if it carries an IRN and a QR code authenticated by the IRP. Without them, you may have trouble claiming input tax credit.
- The e-invoice data feeds into your GST returns and can pre-fill e-way bill Part A.

If an invoice from us has no IRN or QR code, or the GSTIN, quantity or rate is wrong, raise a billing request with the invoice number. Small suppliers below the turnover limit are not required to issue e-invoices.

title: MSME suppliers: the 45-day payment rule and MSME Samadhaan
body:
If you supply goods or services to a buyer and are registered as a micro or small enterprise, the MSMED Act, 2006 protects your payment.

The main rules:
- The buyer must pay within the period agreed in writing, and never later than 45 days from the day the goods or services are accepted (or deemed accepted).
- If the buyer pays late, the buyer owes compound interest with monthly rests at three times the bank rate notified by the RBI (Section 16).
- The delayed-payment provisions are in Sections 15 to 24 of the Act.

Where to complain: the Ministry of MSME's MSME Samadhaan system lets a micro or small enterprise file a delayed-payment case against a buyer before the MSE Facilitation Council (MSEFC) of its state. As of October 2026, new applications are filed on the MSME ODR portal (odr.msme.gov.in). You need a valid Udyam Registration to apply. The council can direct the buyer to pay the dues with interest, and each case is meant to be decided within 90 days.

Before you escalate, check the status of your invoice with us. Many delays happen because the purchase order number is missing on the invoice, the goods receipt is still pending, or the GSTIN or bank details do not match. Signed-in suppliers can look up any of their invoices in this portal. Make sure your Udyam number is recorded on your vendor profile, so that your invoices are tracked under the MSME timeline.

title: Checking the status of a supplier invoice
body:
Suppliers often ask when an invoice will be paid. Here is how to find out quickly.

In this portal: sign in with your supplier account and ask for the status by your own invoice number, for example 'status of invoice MEW/2026/0418'. You will see the purchase order, the date the goods or services were accepted, the due date, the amount and the current status. If the invoice has been paid, you will also see the payment date and the bank UTR.

What the statuses mean:
- Under processing: the invoice is received and matched. Payment will be made by the due date.
- On hold: something is missing, such as the goods receipt (GRN) or service entry, a PO reference, or a GST mismatch. The record shows the reason.
- Paid: the money has been sent. Use the UTR to trace it with your bank.

What helps invoices get paid on time:
- quote the purchase order number on every invoice
- make sure the GSTIN and bank details on the invoice match your vendor profile
- for supplies worth more than Rs 50,000, send the e-way bill number with the dispatch, and the e-invoice IRN if you are covered by e-invoicing

Micro and small suppliers should also read the article on the 45-day payment rule.

title: Tata Astrum hot rolled coils and sheets
body:
Tata Astrum is Tata Steel's brand of hot rolled (HR) coils and sheets for small and medium enterprises. Tata Steel launched it in New Delhi in November 2012. It was the company's first hot rolled brand aimed at SMEs.

Facts from the launch announcement (November 2012):
- Thickness range: 1.6 mm to 16 mm.
- Made at two of Tata Steel's mills in Jamshedpur.
- Target users: SMEs in automotive, earth-moving equipment, railways, fabrication, construction and industrial machinery.
- Sold through authorised distributors. 42 distributors were appointed nationwide at launch. Each one works with Tata Steel-certified service centres, which cut and process the material before supply.

As of October 2026, Tata Astrum is listed on Tata Steel's DigECA platform (digeca.tatasteel.com) together with Tata Steelium (cold rolled), Galvano and GalvaRoS (coated). You can raise an enquiry there or ask an expert.

For current sizes, grades and prices, contact an authorised Tata Astrum distributor or use DigECA. The 2012 numbers above may have changed.

title: Galvano galvanised steel and the DigECA platform
body:
Galvano is Tata Steel's premium galvanised plain (GP) steel. As of October 2026, Tata Steel describes it this way:
- India's first zero-spangle GP brand, with a smooth, even zinc surface
- a strong zinc coating for better corrosion resistance
- produced in line with RoHS standards
- good flatness, uniform mechanical properties for drawing and bending, and tight tolerances

Typical uses: consumer durables, dish antennas, electrical panels, general engineering parts and bus bodies.

DigECA (digeca.tatasteel.com) is Tata Steel's online platform for flat products. It lists Tata Astrum (hot rolled), Tata Steelium (cold rolled), Galvano and GalvaRoS (coated). On DigECA you can:
- send an enquiry, or describe your requirement
- use 'Ask an Expert' for technical questions
- download the Galvano brochure, and read the FAQs and material standards pages
- look at financing through a Tata Capital link ('Avail Finance')

The Galvano page does not publish thickness ranges or prices. Ask through DigECA or an authorised distributor for the sizes, coating mass and lead time you need.

title: Tata Structura, Tata Wiron and Tata Durashine
body:
Besides rebars, home builders and fabricators often buy these Tata Steel brands. All of them are sold on the Tata Steel Aashiyana store and through dealers.

Tata Structura: structural steel hollow sections (tubes) in rectangular, square and circular shapes. They are used for frames, sheds, staircases, railings, gates and roof structures. On Aashiyana, shipping charges apply to Structura orders, as of October 2026.

Tata Wiron: binding wire for tying rebars, and fencing and protection wire products. On Aashiyana, Wiron orders below Rs 15,000 must be collected from the dealer's counter, and shipping charges apply to the rest, as of October 2026.

Tata Durashine: galvanised iron (GI) and colour-coated roofing sheets for homes, sheds and farm buildings. Shipping charges apply on Aashiyana.

Aashiyana also has estimators for rebar, fencing and sheds, which give a rough quantity before you speak to a dealer.

For sizes, thickness and prices in your district, choose your location on Aashiyana or contact a dealer. For help, call 1800 108 8282 or email aashiyana.support@tatasteel.com.

title: Tata Steel customer care, complaints and contact details
body:
Contact details published by Tata Steel, as of October 2026:

- Tata Steel helpline (toll-free): 1800 108 8282. This is also the Tata Tiscon helpline.
- Aashiyana online store: order on call at 0124-6934550, or email aashiyana.support@tatasteel.com. The Help & Support page also has the Aashi chat assistant and a call-back request.
- Complaints and feedback: the Customer Service Request System form on tatasteel.com (Contact us, then Customer feedback and complaints). The form asks which product you bought and where you bought it.
- Registered address, Jamshedpur: Tata Steel Limited, P.O. Bistupur, Jamshedpur 831 001, Jharkhand.
- Long products commercial headquarters: Tata Centre, 43 Jawaharlal Nehru Road, Kolkata 700 071.
- Regional emails for rebar and long products: lpeast@tatasteel.com, lpwest@tatasteel.com, lpsouth@tatasteel.com and lpnorth@tatasteel.com.

When you raise a complaint, have ready: the invoice number, the dealer's name and town, the product and grade, the heat number from the bundle tag (for quality issues), and photos.

Only use numbers published on tatasteel.com, tatatiscon.co.in or aashiyana.tatasteel.com. Tata Steel has warned that unauthorised parties misuse its brand. Do not pay anyone who offers a 'dealership approval' or a discount over the phone.

In this portal you can also open a ticket under Complaints & contact. Our team replies within the hours shown at the top of the page.
